headline: Williams-Sonoma has changed its terms of service to bar customers' AI shopping agents from its websites unless the company gives written permission.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a big retailer shuts out AI shopping agents, a clear sign of the fight over agent shopping, but it is one company and one report.
importance_line: Shoppers who want an AI agent to buy for them are shut out of Williams-Sonoma's sites, and Lauren Willis, a law professor at Loyola Marymount University, calls the terms likely legal for now, but the company had not responded to KQED by publication and its business reason is not explained.
summary: KQED reports that Williams-Sonoma Inc., the parent of Williams Sonoma and Pottery Barn, emailed customers this week new terms of service that bar AI agents and bots from using their accounts or buying on their behalf without the company's written permission, and let it block such tools even when a customer has authorized them. KQED adds that an August federal appeals court ruling in Amazon's suit against Perplexity found that the user, not the AI company, is the one accessing a site when an agent shops, but left retailers free to set rules through their terms of service.
notes: Read in full on KQED. Williams-Sonoma did not respond to KQED.
